# Awesome Open-Source AI Discoveries

Explore creative open-source AI projects for 3D, images, video, music, speech and documents, with upstream examples, setup notes and limitations.

**15 curated entries** · [Browse by task](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/README.md#browse-by-task) · [Suggest a project](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/issues/new?template=suggest-project.yml) · [JSON catalog](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/catalog.json) · [Agent index](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/llms.txt)

Find projects whose result is easy to understand: an image becomes a 3D object, a recording becomes editable notes, or a drawing becomes an animation. Discoveries are editorial picks, not a ranking by stars or a claim that every project is new. Research demos and archived projects are labeled when included.

## Start here

| If you want to... | Explore | Why it belongs |
|---|---|---|
| Turn an image into a 3D starting point | [TripoSR](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/projects/triposr.md) | A concrete visual reconstruction workflow. |
| Turn instrument audio into MIDI | [Basic Pitch](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/projects/basic-pitch.md) | An output you can inspect in a music workflow. |
| Separate a music recording into stems | [Audio Separator](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/projects/audio-separator.md) | A practical audio-processing experiment. |
| Extract masks from images or video | [SAM 2](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/projects/sam2.md) | A reusable visual editing building block. |
| Explore animated character drawings | [Animated Drawings](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/projects/animated-drawings.md) | An archived research demo with a playful result. |

## What is checked

Entries distinguish documentation review from hands-on testing. The initial collection is **documentation-reviewed**: source material was inspected, but these applications have not all been installed or benchmarked by QuicqDev. Each project card records its sources, review date, requirements and a limitation.

Hardware requirements depend on model, quantization, context length and workload. We do not infer RAM needs from parameter counts. Application code, model weights and optional hosted services can have different licenses or costs. Check the linked upstream terms for the configuration you choose.

|---|---|---|

| [Basic Pitch](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/projects/basic-pitch.md) · [upstream](https://github.com/spotify/basic-pitch) · [demo / examples](https://basicpitch.spotify.com/) | Turn an instrumental recording into an editable starting point in a digital audio workstation. | A supported Python environment and compatible audio file; the README links to a browser demo and documents platform-specific model runtimes. |
| [Chatterbox](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/projects/chatterbox.md) · [upstream](https://github.com/resemble-ai/chatterbox) · [demo / examples](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ResembleAI/Chatterbox) | Prototype narration or a speaking character using a voice you own or have permission to use. | Python, the chatterbox-tts package and model downloads; documented generation examples use CUDA, and reference-conditioned generation needs an audio clip. |
| [Kokoro](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/projects/kokoro.md) · [upstream](https://github.com/hexgrad/kokoro) · [demo / examples](https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M/blob/main/SAMPLES.md) | Add local read-aloud audio or draft narration to a small application. | Python, the kokoro package, model and voice assets, and relevant language dependencies; espeak-ng supports some languages and English fallback pronunciation. |

## Frequently asked questions

### Are these hidden gems with few GitHub stars?

Not necessarily. Selection is based on an interesting, understandable result and inspectable source material, not a star threshold. Established projects can be useful discoveries for a new reader.

### Are the online demos guaranteed to stay available?

No. Hosted demos can queue, require login, go offline or impose usage limits. Follow the original repository for current examples and local setup. A README demonstration is different from a live hosted application.

### Can I use the code and model weights commercially?

Check them separately. Open-source code may load weights under different terms, including noncommercial conditions. Relevant distinctions are noted in project cards, with the upstream source as the authority.

### Why include an archived project?

An archived research demo can still illustrate a useful creative technique. Its archived status is stated in the caveat, and it should not be mistaken for a maintained application. Prefer active alternatives for ongoing workflows.

## How to contribute

Add a useful project, correct an outdated entry, or submit a reproducible compatibility report. Edit `catalog.json` and run `python scripts/build.py`; the README, project cards and agent index are generated from that source. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for selection criteria and the field format.

Automated checks validate the catalog on changes and check external links weekly. A reachable link does not establish that software works, is secure, or fits your hardware. Failed and inconclusive checks need review; metadata checks never advance an editorial review date.

## For agents and search tools

Read the [structured catalog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/main/catalog.json), its [schema](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/catalog.schema.json), or the compact [llms.txt index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/main/llms.txt). Each entry has a stable ID, category, use case, prerequisites, caveat, evidence level and source URLs. Cite the upstream project for its capabilities and this collection for editorial comparisons.

`llms.txt` is a navigation aid, not a promise of inclusion in any search engine or model response. Unknown requirements remain unknown; documentation-reviewed entries must not be described as personally tested.

# TripoSR: Turn an object illustration into a mesh for an early game-asset or product-visualization prototype

Reconstruct a 3D object from one image, with command-line inference and a local Gradio interface.

## Demo or examples

[Explore the creator’s demo or examples](https://github.com/VAST-AI-Research/TripoSR/tree/main/figures)

Upstream examples, not live demo

[Upstream project](https://github.com/VAST-AI-Research/TripoSR) · [Back to collection](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/README.md#3d-and-depth)

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Category | 3D and depth |
| Use case | Turn an object illustration into a mesh for an early game-asset or product-visualization prototype. |
| Requirements | Python, PyTorch, downloaded model weights and the repository dependencies; CUDA setup must match the installed PyTorch build when using GPU acceleration. |
| Caveat | Treat reconstructed geometry as a starting point to inspect and edit; a single input view cannot establish the object's unseen surfaces. |
| Evidence | documentation-reviewed |
| Documentation reviewed | 2026-09-12 |

## Sources and getting started

[Source 1](https://github.com/VAST-AI-Research/TripoSR)

Use the upstream documentation for installation and examples. We link to the creator’s demonstrations rather than presenting their work as our own. Confirm current software and model terms before use.

## Improve this entry

Submit a correction or a compatibility report through [the contribution guide](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). Entry ID: `triposr`.


# MoGe: Explore a room photo as a 3D scene or create geometry inputs for a visual prototype

Estimate scene geometry from a photograph and export depth maps, point clouds or meshes; MoGe-2 also provides metric-scale predictions.

## Demo or examples

[Explore the creator’s demo or examples](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Ruicheng/MoGe-2)

Official MoGe-2 interactive demo; hosted availability may vary and compute may queue.

[Upstream project](https://github.com/microsoft/MoGe) · [Back to collection](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/README.md#3d-and-depth)

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Category | 3D and depth |
| Use case | Explore a room photo as a 3D scene or create geometry inputs for a visual prototype. |
| Requirements | Python dependencies and a matching pretrained checkpoint; the documented inference example uses a CUDA device, and a local Gradio demo is included. |
| Caveat | Match the model version and checkpoint; the current MoGe-3 instructions require an explicit checkpoint path. Inspect inferred geometry before treating it as a measurement. |
| Evidence | documentation-reviewed |
| Documentation reviewed | 2026-09-12 |

## Sources and getting started

[Source 1](https://github.com/microsoft/MoGe) · [Source 2](https://github.com/microsoft/MoGe/blob/main/README.md)

Use the upstream documentation for installation and examples. We link to the creator’s demonstrations rather than presenting their work as our own. Confirm current software and model terms before use.

## Improve this entry

Submit a correction or a compatibility report through [the contribution guide](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). Entry ID: `moge`.


# Depth Anything V2: Produce depth masks for parallax experiments, depth-aware compositing or computer-vision prototypes

Predict depth maps from images or videos, with several checkpoint sizes and a Gradio demo.

[Explore the creator’s demo or examples](https://huggingface.co/spaces/depth-anything/Depth-Anything-V2)

Official interactive demo; hosted availability may vary and compute may queue.

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Category | 3D and depth |
| Use case | Produce depth masks for parallax experiments, depth-aware compositing or computer-vision prototypes. |
| Requirements | Python, PyTorch and a downloaded checkpoint; the example selects CUDA, Apple MPS or CPU according to availability. |
| Caveat | Default checkpoints estimate relative depth. Small-model weights use Apache-2.0, while larger variants carry noncommercial terms; choose the checkpoint deliberately. |
| Evidence | documentation-reviewed |
| Documentation reviewed | 2026-09-12 |

## Sources and getting started

[Source 1](https://github.com/DepthAnything/Depth-Anything-V2)

# SAM 2: Prototype object cutouts, video masking or annotation tools from user-supplied prompts

Select objects in images and propagate segmentation masks through video, with example notebooks and web-demo source.

## Demo or examples

[Explore the creator’s demo or examples](https://sam2.metademolab.com/)

Official interactive demo; requires JavaScript. Hosted availability may vary and compute may queue.

[Upstream project](https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam2) · [Back to collection](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/README.md#images-and-video)

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Category | Images and video |
| Use case | Prototype object cutouts, video masking or annotation tools from user-supplied prompts. |
| Requirements | Python, compatible PyTorch and TorchVision versions, and a model checkpoint; the documented installation targets a GPU machine and recommends WSL for Windows. |
| Caveat | Match checkpoint and code versions. A failed optional CUDA extension build can limit post-processing, and masks still need review for the intended footage. |
| Evidence | documentation-reviewed |
| Documentation reviewed | 2026-09-12 |

## Sources and getting started

[Source 1](https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam2)

Use the upstream documentation for installation and examples. We link to the creator’s demonstrations rather than presenting their work as our own. Confirm current software and model terms before use.

# BiRefNet: Build a subject-cutout workflow or experiment with placing text behind a foreground subject

Extract detailed foreground masks using pretrained models for general segmentation, portraits and image matting.

## Demo or examples

[Explore the creator’s demo or examples](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet_demo)

Official interactive demo; hosted availability may vary and compute may queue.

[Upstream project](https://github.com/ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet) · [Back to collection](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/README.md#images-and-video)

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Category | Images and video |
| Use case | Build a subject-cutout workflow or experiment with placing text behind a foreground subject. |
| Requirements | A Python inference environment and task-appropriate weights; upstream supplies PyTorch examples, notebooks and ONNX export guidance. |
| Caveat | Matting and binary segmentation models solve different problems. Check the chosen weights and preprocessing instead of assuming all model variants behave alike. |
| Evidence | documentation-reviewed |
| Documentation reviewed | 2026-09-12 |

## Sources and getting started

[Source 1](https://github.com/ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet)

Use the upstream documentation for installation and examples. We link to the creator’s demonstrations rather than presenting their work as our own. Confirm current software and model terms before use.

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Category | Images and video |
| Use case | Enlarge a small illustration or pixelated image before using it in a presentation or design draft. |
| Requirements | Install the desktop release for your operating system and use a Vulkan-compatible GPU; many integrated GPUs are unsupported. |
| Caveat | Upscaling synthesizes plausible detail. Upstream explicitly says it is not a tool for restoring focus to a completely blurred image. |

# Audio Separator: Create practice tracks or isolate parts of a recording you are authorized to process

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Category | Music and speech |
| Use case | Create practice tracks or isolate parts of a recording you are authorized to process. |
| Requirements | Python or Docker, FFmpeg and a selected separation model; upstream documents CPU, CUDA and Apple Silicon options. |
| Caveat | Available stems and accelerator support vary by model. Listen for residual bleed and artifacts, and check the selected model's terms before redistribution. |
| Evidence | documentation-reviewed |
| Documentation reviewed | 2026-09-12 |

## Sources and getting started

[Source 1](https://github.com/nomadkaraoke/python-audio-separator)

# Basic Pitch: Turn an instrumental recording into an editable starting point in a digital audio workstation

Convert an audio performance into MIDI notes with pitch bends using Spotify's music-transcription library.

## Demo or examples

[Explore the creator’s demo or examples](https://basicpitch.spotify.com/)

Official browser demo; hosted availability may vary. Browser support and the input recording affect the experience.

[Upstream project](https://github.com/spotify/basic-pitch) · [Back to collection](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/README.md#music-and-speech)

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Category | Music and speech |
| Use case | Turn an instrumental recording into an editable starting point in a digital audio workstation. |
| Requirements | A supported Python environment and compatible audio file; the README links to a browser demo and documents platform-specific model runtimes. |
| Caveat | Upstream says transcription works best on one instrument at a time. Plan to review and correct notes from a dense mix. |
| Evidence | documentation-reviewed |
| Documentation reviewed | 2026-09-12 |

## Sources and getting started

# Chatterbox: Prototype narration or a speaking character using a voice you own or have permission to use

A family of text-to-speech models with expressive controls, multilingual options and reference-audio voice conditioning.

## Demo or examples

[Explore the creator’s demo or examples](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ResembleAI/Chatterbox)

Official Chatterbox demo linked by upstream; hosted availability may vary and compute may queue. Other model variants have separate demos.

[Upstream project](https://github.com/resemble-ai/chatterbox) · [Back to collection](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/README.md#music-and-speech)

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Category | Music and speech |
| Use case | Prototype narration or a speaking character using a voice you own or have permission to use. |
| Requirements | Python, the chatterbox-tts package and model downloads; documented generation examples use CUDA, and reference-conditioned generation needs an audio clip. |
| Caveat | Model variants support different controls and languages. Reference-language mismatch can affect accent, and generated audio includes the project's watermarking mechanism. |
| Evidence | documentation-reviewed |
| Documentation reviewed | 2026-09-12 |

## Sources and getting started

[Source 1](https://github.com/resemble-ai/chatterbox)

# Kokoro: Add local read-aloud audio or draft narration to a small application

A Python inference library for an open-weight text-to-speech model, with selectable voices and audio-file export examples.

## Demo or examples

[Explore the creator’s demo or examples](https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M/blob/main/SAMPLES.md)

Upstream examples, not live demo

[Upstream project](https://github.com/hexgrad/kokoro) · [Back to collection](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/README.md#music-and-speech)

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Category | Music and speech |
| Use case | Add local read-aloud audio or draft narration to a small application. |
| Requirements | Python, the kokoro package, model and voice assets, and relevant language dependencies; espeak-ng supports some languages and English fallback pronunciation. |
| Caveat | Language and voice selection must match the pipeline. Review pronunciation and pacing on real text before using the output as finished narration. |
| Evidence | documentation-reviewed |
| Documentation reviewed | 2026-09-12 |

## Sources and getting started

[Source 1](https://github.com/hexgrad/kokoro)

Use the upstream documentation for installation and examples. We link to the creator’s demonstrations rather than presenting their work as our own. Confirm current software and model terms before use.

# Docling: Prepare a collection of reports for search, retrieval or a document-processing application

Convert PDFs and other document formats into structured content, including Markdown and JSON, with layout, table and OCR support.

## Demo or examples

[Explore the creator’s demo or examples](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/examples/)

Upstream examples, not live demo

[Upstream project](https://github.com/docling-project/docling) · [Back to collection](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/README.md#documents-and-knowledge)

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Category | Documents and knowledge |
| Use case | Prepare a collection of reports for search, retrieval or a document-processing application. |
| Requirements | A supported Python environment and the docling package; download the models required by the selected local parsing pipeline. |
| Caveat | Optional model licenses differ from the code license. Spot-check tables, formulas and reading order before indexing extracted content. |
| Evidence | documentation-reviewed |
| Documentation reviewed | 2026-09-12 |

## Sources and getting started

[Source 1](https://github.com/docling-project/docling)

Use the upstream documentation for installation and examples. We link to the creator’s demonstrations rather than presenting their work as our own. Confirm current software and model terms before use.

# Surya: Explore how a document parser identifies text, tables and page structure in a scanned document

Perform OCR, page-layout analysis, reading-order detection and table recognition, with annotated examples for different document types.

## Demo or examples

[Explore the creator’s demo or examples](https://github.com/datalab-to/surya#examples)

Upstream examples, not live demo

[Upstream project](https://github.com/datalab-to/surya) · [Back to collection](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-open-source-ai-discoveries/blob/main/README.md#documents-and-knowledge)

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Category | Documents and knowledge |
| Use case | Explore how a document parser identifies text, tables and page structure in a scanned document. |
| Requirements | Python and surya-ocr plus an inference backend: the reviewed instructions use vLLM for NVIDIA GPUs or llama.cpp for CPU and Apple Silicon. |
| Caveat | The code and model weights have different licenses; broader commercial use of the weights can require a separate license. Review the current model terms before deployment. |
| Evidence | documentation-reviewed |
| Documentation reviewed | 2026-09-12 |

## Sources and getting started

[Source 1](https://github.com/datalab-to/surya)

Use the upstream documentation for installation and examples. We link to the creator’s demonstrations rather than presenting their work as our own. Confirm current software and model terms before use.
